newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cypriot leader to attend further Cyprus talks.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriot leader to attend further Cyprus talks.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot officials said on Monday their leader Rauf Denktash would attend further talks with Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides this month to try to resolve the dispute splitting the island.

"The cabinet...has reached the decision to attend the talks planned to be held in Switzerland on August 11," Turkish Cypriot official Dervish Eroglu told reporters after a meeting of officials from the breakaway northern Cypriot state.
Manolis Christofides, spokesman for the Greek Cypriot-led government, said he welcomed Denktash's decision to attend the talks.
"In good faith we are willing to discuss all aspects of the Cyprus problem to find a solution to each of them," he said.

Clerides and Denktash met in New York state last month under the auspices of the United Nations for the first time in three years in an attempt to revive stalled negotiations on Cypriot reunification as a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation.
Denktash had said previously that future talks could be jeopardised by a bid to give European Union membership to the Greek Cypriot-led government in the south of the island.

The two have held follow-up talks in Nicosia since the New York meeting in which they reached an agreement that could lead to the opening of unmarked graves of people missing in hostilities between Cyprus's Greek and Turkish communities.
They are set to meet in Montreux, Switzerland, this month.
Turkey invaded the northern third of Cyprus in 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup backed by the military then ruling Greece. Around 30,000 Turkish troops are stationed there.
A Turkish Cypriot state was declared in 1983 but is recognised only by Ankara.
